newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: OLYMPICS-HAVELANGE HAILS BUENOS AIRES 2004 OLYMPIC BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-HAVELANGE HAILS BUENOS AIRES 2004 OLYMPIC BID.

text.p: Joao Havelange, the Brazil-born president of the international football body FIFA, Wednesday openly endorsed Argentina's bid to host the 2004 Olympic Games.

"I knew of Buenos Aires' bid and thought it was good. But when I saw it myself I was thrilled -- the proposal is the most solid and feasible one to organise the Olympic Games," Havelange said in a news conference in Argentina.

"When Rio de Janeiro lost the candidacy I immediately threw my support behind Argentina, because that way I get to keep the ball," he said. "I know Buenos Aires well, it has long been my second home. I even spent my honeymoon here and that was a long time ago."
Havelange, who was granted the country's highest decoration, the Mayor Order for Merit, by President Carlos Menem Tuesday, showered praise on Argentina.
"It is a country in which all sports must be respected, admired and applauded," he said.
Havelange also said he backed the candidacy of Argentine Football Association (AFA) president Julio Grondona as his successor when he retires next year.

"Julio is a great friend, he's like my brother. He's a great leader who may continue along the road I took many years ago if he is elected president of FIFA," he said. "But before that we must fight, especially against European countries who want to place their candidates at the helm of world football."
Regarding the advantages Argentina offers as host of the Olympic Games, Havelange noted athletes would not have to travel long distances to participate in events.

"When I was in Barcelona in 1992 I had to travel 200 km to see the rowing competition. In Buenos Aires you only have to walk five minutes to see the race. And this is something that surely will be taken into account at voting time," he said.
Havelange, who caught typhoid fever in 1943 and weighed only 35 kilos, took part in the Berlin 1936 Olympics as a member of Brazil's swimming team.

Buenos Aires was shortlisted in March along with Athens, Cape Town, Rome and Stockhold from among 11 candidates after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) studied a detailed technical report of each bid. The final vote will be made September 5.
Rio de Janeiro was dropped from the list, along with Istanbul, Lille, San Juan, Seville and St Petersburg.
